title: Free groups as words: the set-quotient of lists of letters and formal inverses is the free group
author: The Univalent Foundations Program

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled theorem at source lines 1638-1647, Theorem 6.11.7: the set-quotient of lst(A+A) by the two cancellation relations is again the free group on A. The author's 31-line proof (source lines 1648-1678) is a full construction of the group structure on a quotient, not a citation of the abstract universal property: the multiplication is defined by double quotient recursion and the unit and associativity laws are proved by quotient induction (lines 1650-1652), the inverse is built from a reverse operation on lists and checked against the relations (lines 1654-1660), and the inverse law i(x) `ct` x = e is reduced first by quotient induction and then by list induction, with the inductive case carried out explicitly at lines 1663-1670 and further concatenation lemmas deliberately omitted at line 1671. The final universal property is then checked on the quotient rather than assumed.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of Theorem 6.11.7, retained line for line

contexts.label: the author's lead-in paragraph introducing lists of A + A as words for the free group, with the formal inverse written as a hat
